title: Digit restoration during a recorded step
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $Q,T,S$ be types with decidable equality, let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Boolean Turing machine with states in $Q$, let $u:T\times\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$, and let $N$ be a two-work-tape Boolean Turing machine with states in $S$, with designated states $s_0,s_1\in S$. For a Boolean input word $x$, a configuration $d$ of the four-tape recording machine on the input obtained by embedding each bit of $x$ as a digit, a word $b$ over the recording alphabet, record data $D$, and natural numbers $W,q,p$, suppose $q+1<2^W$ and $p=q+1$ if the recorded native move is right, while $p=q$ otherwise. Then the recording machine has a run of some length $t\le 4W+6$ from the snapshot with control in the forward complementing phase, tape 0 head offset zero, auxiliary words $b$ and the counter word obtained by applying the fixed-width decrement operation $q+1$ times to $W$ ones and embedding its bits as digits, to the snapshot with control in the restoration phase at state $s_0$, tape 0 head offset zero, and auxiliary words $b$ and the width-$W$ binary expansion of $p$ embedded as digits. Throughout this run, neither designated verdict state is reached before time $t$, and every work-tape head remains within distance $W+1$ of its initial position in $d$.

$N$ is a two-tape Boolean machine with state type $S$

$p=q+1$ when the native move is right, and $p=q$ otherwise
